source.title: A2SG:Adaptive and Asymmetric Surrogate Gradients for Training Deep Spiking Neural Networks
source.authors: Ye-Chan Kang; Y. Kweon; Min-Yeong Seo; Sohee Park; Yeonguk Jeon; Jongkil Park; H. Jang; Jaewook Kim; Yeonjoo Jeong; Su-Yoon Lee; Seongsik Park

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares surrogate-gradient training methods and measures Fisher information eigenvalues alongside test accuracy, providing a conceptual test of whether a measured landscape property accompanies generalization performance. It does not test the claim versions’ specified settings or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy comparisons and FIM eigenvalue results for surrogate-gradient methods. The FIM results are figure-only; cited results from other work are excluded. The study does not measure train-test gaps, random-label memorization, or magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness.
record.test_reason: The study uses the broad flat-minima/generalization rationale to develop surrogate gradients for spiking networks, but tests none of V1–V8. FIM eigenvalues and test accuracy do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with train–test gaps. Adaptive surrogate gradients are not an adaptive-versus-SGD optimizer comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: A2 SG reduces gradient variability, stabilizes optimization, encourages flatter solutions, and improves accuracy, robustness, and efficiency across tested SNN tasks. Efficiency refers principally to spike counts and estimated energy; training incurs additional overhead, about 15% for VGG16 at four timesteps.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains spiking neural networks using adaptive and asymmetric surrogate gradients; it does not use the claim versions’ specified interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported FIM eigenvalue comparison varies by surrogate-gradient function and layer; the paper states Arctan is comparable to BOX and TRI, while ASY and A2 SG have substantially lower values.

fits_no_version.finding: For spiking VGG16 on CIFAR10, A2 SG reaches 95.29±0.04% test accuracy versus 94.84±0.05% for BOX. The text also reports lower FIM eigenvalues for A2 SG, with ASY and A2 SG below BOX, TRI, and Arctan.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Surrogate-gradient design in the tested spiking networks affects held-out accuracy and measured FIM curvature.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The reported FIM comparisons are figures without numeric values or uncertainty. The paper does not report training error or train-test gaps, and the FIM results do not measure the magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness specified in V7.
record.rows_left_out: Other test-accuracy comparisons across datasets, architectures, methods, and ablations were omitted because they do not report training error or a train-test gap; they are reported in Tables 1–6 and 7–10 and Tables A3–A6. Figure-only SGV and TGC comparisons were omitted because they measure gradient variation or alignment rather than a version’s stated behavior or measure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its ranking of train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains no additional result testing V1–V8. Different batch sizes across differently sized ImageNet models do not isolate a batch-size effect. Spike-deletion robustness is not a dropout-training experiment.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and their tuning dependence.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, train-test gaps among models at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
